Conductive hearing loss.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Conductive hearing loss.question: This can be an isolated phenomenon or may occur as part of a syndrome where development of the 1st and 2nd branchial arches is seen, such as in Goldenhar syndrome, Treacher Collins syndrome, _____, etc

Conductive hearing loss.question: It is managed by any of various methods of ear clearing manoeuvres to equalize the pressures, like swallowing, yawning, or the _____ manoeuvre
Conductive hearing loss.fact: It is managed by any of various methods of ear clearing manoeuvres to equalize the pressures, like swallowing, yawning, or the Valsalva manoeuvre.

Conductive hearing loss.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Conductive hearing loss.question: With a one-sided conductive component, the combined use of both the _____ and Rinne tests is useful
Conductive hearing loss.fact: With a one-sided conductive component, the combined use of both the Weber and Rinne tests is useful. If the Weber test is used, in which a vibrating tuning fork is touched to the midline of the forehead, the person will hear the sound more loudly in the affected ear because background noise does not mask the hearing on this side.

Contact dermatitis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Contact dermatitis.question: The _____ was Inflammation from allergen or irritant exposure.
Contact dermatitis.fact: Contact dermatitis is a type of acute or chronic inflammation of the skin caused by exposure to chemical or physical agents. Symptoms of contact dermatitis can include itchy or dry skin, a red rash, bumps, blisters, or swelling.

Contact dermatitis.question: Allergens include nickel, gold, Balsam of Peru (_____ pereirae), chromium, and the oily coating from plants of the genus Toxicodendron, such as poison ivy, poison oak, and poison sumac

Contact dermatitis.fact: The top three allergens found in patch tests from 2005 to 2006 were: nickel sulfate (19.0%), Myroxylon pereirae (Balsam of Peru, 11.9%), and fragrance mix I (11.5%).

Crista ampullaris.question: The _____ was Sensory organ in the inner ear.
Crista ampullaris.fact: The crista ampullaris is the sensory organ of rotation. The function of the crista ampullaris is to sense angular acceleration and deceleration.

Appendix of testis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Appendix of testis.question: The _____ was Part of the testis.
Appendix of testis.fact: Torsion of the appendix of testis occurs at ages 0–15 years, with a mean at 10 years, which is similar to that of testicular torsion.

Appendix of testis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Appendix of testis.question: The appendix testis (or hydatid of _____) is a vestigial remnant of the Müllerian duct, present on the upper pole of the testis and attached to the tunica vaginalis
Appendix of testis.fact: The appendix testis (or hydatid of Morgagni) is a vestigial remnant of the Müllerian duct, present on the upper pole of the testis and attached to the tunica vaginalis.

Appendix of testis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Appendix of testis.question: It is present about _____ of the time
Appendix of testis.fact: It is present about 90% of the time.

Appendix of the epididymis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Appendix of the epididymis.question: This structure is derived from the _____ duct (mesonephric duct) as opposed to the appendix testis which is derived from the Müllerian duct (paramesonephric duct) remnant
Appendix of the epididymis.fact: This structure is derived from the Wolffian duct (mesonephric duct) as opposed to the appendix testis which is derived from the Müllerian duct (paramesonephric duct) remnant.

Artery of bulb of penis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Artery of bulb of penis.question: The _____ was Blood vessel.
Artery of bulb of penis.fact: The artery of bulb of penis (artery of the urethral bulb or bulbourethral artery) is a short artery of large caliber which arises from the internal pudendal artery between the two layers of fascia (the superior and inferior) of the urogenital diaphragm.

Blood–testis barrier.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Blood–testis barrier.question: The _____ was Physical barrier between the blood vessels and the seminiferous tubules of animal testes.
Blood–testis barrier.fact: The blood–testis barrier is a physical barrier between the blood vessels and the seminiferous tubules of the animal testes.

Blood–testis barrier.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Blood–testis barrier.question: A more correct term is the _____ cell barrier (SCB)
Blood–testis barrier.fact: The name "blood-testis barrier" is misleading as it is not a blood-organ barrier in a strict sense, but is formed between Sertoli cells of the seminiferous tubule and isolates the further developed stages of germ cells from the blood. A more correct term is the Sertoli cell barrier (SCB).

Blood–testis barrier.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Blood–testis barrier.question: For the visualization of the actin fibers within the seminiferous tubules see _____ et al.'s immunofluorescence studies
Blood–testis barrier.fact: For the visualization of the actin fibers within the seminiferous tubules see Sharma et al.'s immunofluorescence studies.

Blood–testis barrier.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Blood–testis barrier.question: Some proteins pass from _____ cells to Leydig cells to function in a paracrine fashion
Blood–testis barrier.fact: Some proteins pass from Sertoli cells to Leydig cells to function in a paracrine fashion.

Body of penis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Body of penis.question: The _____ was Part of the penis located outside of the pelvic cavity.
Body of penis.fact: The body or shaft of the penis is the free portion of the human penis that is located outside of the pelvic cavity. It is the continuation of the internal root, which is embedded in the pelvis and extends to the glans.

Body of penis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Body of penis.question: The body is ensheathed by fascia, which includes tunica albuginea, _____'s fascia, dermis, and skin
Body of penis.fact: The body is ensheathed by fascia, which includes tunica albuginea, Buck's fascia, dermis, and skin.

Buck's fascia.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Buck's fascia.question: The _____ was Fascia in the penis.
Buck's fascia.fact: Buck's fascia (deep fascia of the penis, Gallaudet's fascia or fascia of the penis) is a layer of deep fascia covering the three erectile bodies of the penis.

Bulb of penis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Bulb of penis.question: The _____ was Flare of the urethra tissue at the base of the human biological male sex organ.
Bulb of penis.fact: The bulb of penis is the proximal/posterior bulged end of the (unpaired median) corpus spongiosum penis. Proximally/posteriorly, the bulb of penis extends towards the perineal body.

Bulbourethral gland.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Bulbourethral gland.question: The _____ was Gland in males to help with sperm health.
Bulbourethral gland.fact: The bulbourethral glands or Cowper's glands (named after the English anatomist William Cowper KOO-pər) are two small exocrine and accessory glands in the reproductive system of many male mammals. The bulbourethral glands are responsible for producing a pre-ejaculate fluid called Cowper's fluid (known colloquially as pre-cum), which is secreted during sexual arousal, neutralizing the acidity of the urethra in preparation for the passage of sperm cells.

Bulbourethral gland.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Bulbourethral gland.question: They are homologous to _____'s glands in females
Bulbourethral gland.fact: They are homologous to Bartholin's glands in females.

Corpus cavernosum penis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Corpus cavernosum penis.question: The _____ was Sponge-like region of erectile tissue.
Corpus cavernosum penis.fact: A corpus cavernosum penis (singular) (from Latin, characterised by cavities, or hollows, of the penis, pl.: corpora cavernosa penium) is one of a pair of sponge-like regions of erectile tissue, which contain most of the blood in the penis during an erection in several species of mammals.

Corpus cavernosum penis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Corpus cavernosum penis.question: A little blood enters the corpus spongiosum; the remainder engorges the corpora cavernosa, which expand to hold _____ of the blood involved in an erection, increasing both in length and in diameter
Corpus cavernosum penis.fact: A little blood enters the corpus spongiosum; the remainder engorges the corpora cavernosa, which expand to hold 90% of the blood involved in an erection, increasing both in length and in diameter.

Corona of glans penis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Corona of glans penis.question: The _____ was Flare above the sulcus of the human penis.
Corona of glans penis.fact: The corona of glans penis (or, directly from the Latin, the corona glandis penis) or penis crown refers to the rounded projecting border or flare that forms at the base of the glans in human males.

Cremaster muscle.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Cremaster muscle.question: The _____ was Muscle covering the testicles and spermatic cords.
Cremaster muscle.fact: The cremaster muscle is a paired structure made of thin layers of striated and smooth muscle that covers the testicles and the spermatic cords in human males.

Cremaster muscle.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Cremaster muscle.question: The ideal temperature for human sperm development is around 34.5-35 degrees _____, which is about 2-2.5 degrees Celsius below body temperature
Cremaster muscle.fact: The ideal temperature for human sperm development is around 34.5-35 degrees Celsius, which is about 2-2.5 degrees Celsius below body temperature.

Cremaster muscle.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Cremaster muscle.question: The cremaster can also be contracted voluntarily, by performing _____ (which somehow contracts the cremaster), or by flexing and tightening the abdominal muscles
Cremaster muscle.fact: The cremaster can also be contracted voluntarily, by performing Kegels (which somehow contracts the cremaster), or by flexing and tightening the abdominal muscles.

Cremaster muscle.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Cremaster muscle.question: Treatment for these spasms ranges from minor surgery to injection with _____ A toxin to the regular application of heat to relax the muscle
Cremaster muscle.fact: Treatment for these spasms ranges from minor surgery to injection with Botulinum A toxin to the regular application of heat to relax the muscle.

Crus of penis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Crus of penis.question: The _____ was Internal base of the human biological male sex organ.
Crus of penis.fact: The two crura of penis (one crus on each side) constitute the root of penis along with the bulb of penis. The two crura flank the bulb – one to each side of the bulb.

Dartos fascia.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Dartos fascia.question: The _____ was Layer of tissue.
Dartos fascia.fact: The dartos fascia, dartos tunic or simply dartos is a layer of connective tissue found in the penile shaft, foreskin and scrotum.

Dartos fascia.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Dartos fascia.question: In addition to being continuous with itself between the scrotum and the penis, it is also continuous with _____' fascia of the perineum and Scarpa's fascia of the abdomen
Dartos fascia.fact: In addition to being continuous with itself between the scrotum and the penis, it is also continuous with Colles' fascia of the perineum and Scarpa's fascia of the abdomen.

Dartos fascia.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Dartos fascia.question: The dartos lies just below the skin, which places it just superficial to the external spermatic fascia in the scrotum and to _____'s fascia in the penile shaft
Dartos fascia.fact: The dartos lies just below the skin, which places it just superficial to the external spermatic fascia in the scrotum and to Buck's fascia in the penile shaft.

Dorsal artery of the penis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Dorsal artery of the penis.question: The _____ was Artery of the penis.
Dorsal artery of the penis.fact: The dorsal artery of the penis is a bilaterally paired terminal branch of the internal pudendal artery which passes upon the dorsum of the penis to the base of the glans penis, where it unites with its contralateral partner and supply the glans and foreskin. The dorsal artery of the penis provides blood supply to the skin and fascia of the penis (including the foreskin), and the erectile tissues of the penis (especially the glans penis).

Dorsal nerve of the penis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Dorsal nerve of the penis.question: The _____ was Deepest division of the pudendal nerve.
Dorsal nerve of the penis.fact: The dorsal nerve of the penis is the deepest of three divisions of the pudendal nerve; it accompanies the internal pudendal artery along the ramus of the ischium; it then runs forward along the margin of the inferior ramus of the pubis, between the superior and inferior layers of the fascia of the urogenital diaphragm.

Efferent ducts.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Efferent ducts.question: The _____ was Testicular anatomical structure.
Efferent ducts.fact: The efferent ducts (also efferent ductules, ductuli efferentes, ductus efferentes, or vasa efferentia) connect the rete testis with the initial section of the epididymis. In humans and other large mammals, there are approximately 15 to 20 efferent ducts, which also occupy nearly one-third of the head of the epididymis.

Ejaculatory duct.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Ejaculatory duct.question: The _____ was Male anatomical structures.
Ejaculatory duct.fact: The ejaculatory ducts (ductus ejaculatorii) are paired structures in the male reproductive system. Each ejaculatory duct is formed by the union of the vas deferens with the duct of the seminal vesicle.

Epididymis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Epididymis.question: The _____ was Tube that connects a testicle to a vas deferens.
Epididymis.fact: The epididymis (; pl.: epididymides or ) is an elongated tubular genital organ attached to the posterior side of each one of the two male reproductive glands, the testicles. The epididymis connects the testicle to the vas deferens in the male reproductive system.

Epididymis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Epididymis.question: The major cell types in the epithelium are: _____ cells: columnar cells that, with the basal cells, form the majority of the epithelium
Epididymis.fact: The major cell types in the epithelium are: Principal cells: columnar cells that, with the basal cells, form the majority of the epithelium.

Epididymis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy

External spermatic fascia.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy

External spermatic fascia.fact: The external spermatic fascia (intercrural or intercolumnar fascia) is a thin membrane, prolonged downward around the surface of the spermatic cord and testis.

External sphincter muscle of male urethr.fact: The external sphincter muscle of the male urethra, also sphincter urethrae membranaceae, sphincter urethrae externus, surrounds the whole length of the membranous urethra, and is enclosed in the fascia of the urogenital diaphragm. Cleavage (embryo).question: Sack's Law: _____ cells are of equal size; and successive planes of division are at right angles to one another

Tentacle.question: The _____ was Varied organ found in many animals and used for palpation and manipulation.

Anterior clinoid process.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Anterior clinoid process.question: The _____ was Portion of brain anatomy.
Anterior clinoid process.fact: The anterior clinoid process is a posterior projection of the sphenoid bone at the junction of the medial end of either lesser wing of sphenoid bone with the body of sphenoid bone.

Anterior clinoid process.question: The term may also come from the _____ root klinein or the Latin clinare, both meaning "sloped" as in "inclined"

Anterior ethmoidal foramen.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Anterior ethmoidal foramen.question: The _____ was Opening in the ethmoid bone in the skull.
Anterior ethmoidal foramen.fact: The anterior ethmoidal foramen is a small opening in the ethmoid bone in the skull. The anterior ethmoidal foramen, situated about the middle of the lateral margin of the olfactory groove, transmits the anterior ethmoidal artery, vein and nerve.

Basilar part of occipital bone.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Basilar part of occipital bone.question: The _____ was Section of the main skull bone that extends forward and upward.
Basilar part of occipital bone.fact: The basilar part of the occipital bone extends forward and upward from the foramen magnum, and presents in front an area more or less quadrilateral in outline. In the young skull, this area is rough and uneven, and is joined to the body of the sphenoid by a plate of cartilage.

Brow ridge.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Brow ridge.question: The _____ was Bony ridge located above the eye sockets of all primates.
Brow ridge.fact: The brow ridge, or supraorbital ridge called superciliary arch in medicine, is a bony ridge located above the eye sockets of all primates and some other animals.

Brow ridge.question: In medicine, the term arcus superciliaris (Latin) or the _____ translation superciliary arch

Carotid canal.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Carotid canal.question: The _____ was Passage in the skull's temporal bone.
Carotid canal.fact: The carotid canal is a passage in the petrous part of the temporal bone of the skull through which the internal carotid artery and its internal carotid (nervous) plexus pass from the neck into (the middle cranial fossa of) the cranial cavity.

Carotid groove.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Carotid groove.question: The _____ was Groove in the sphenoid bone.
Carotid groove.fact: The carotid groove is an anatomical groove in the sphenoid bone located above the attachment of each great wing of the sphenoid bone.

Chiasmatic groove.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Chiasmatic groove.question: The _____ was Groove on the sphenoid bone of the skull.
Chiasmatic groove.fact: The chiasmatic groove (chiasmatic sulcus, optic groove, prechiasmatic sulcus) is a transverse groove upon the superior aspect of the body of sphenoid bone within the middle cranial fossa. The optic chiasm is situated superior and quite posterior to the chiasmatic groove (and not against the groove as the name suggests).

Clivus (anatomy).subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Clivus (anatomy).question: The _____ was Bony part of the skull base.
Clivus (anatomy).fact: The clivus (, Latin for "slope") or Blumenbach's clivus is a part of the occipital bone at the base of the skull, extending anteriorly from the foramen magnum. It is related to the pons and the abducens nerve (CN VI).

Clivus (anatomy).subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Clivus (anatomy).question: The clivus (, Latin for "slope") or _____'s clivus is a part of the occipital bone at the base of the skull, extending anteriorly from the foramen magnum
Clivus (anatomy).fact: The clivus (, Latin for "slope") or Blumenbach's clivus is a part of the occipital bone at the base of the skull, extending anteriorly from the foramen magnum.

Clivus (anatomy).subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Clivus (anatomy).question: It is medial to the foramen lacerum and proximal to the anastomosis of the internal carotid artery with the _____ of Willis
Clivus (anatomy).fact: It is medial to the foramen lacerum and proximal to the anastomosis of the internal carotid artery with the Circle of Willis.

Clivus (anatomy).subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Clivus (anatomy).question: Variations of the clivus include fossa navicularis magna, craniopharyngeal canal, canalis basilaris medianus, and transverse basilar fissure (_____'s fissure)
Clivus (anatomy).fact: Variations of the clivus include fossa navicularis magna, craniopharyngeal canal, canalis basilaris medianus, and transverse basilar fissure (Saucer's fissure).

Clivus (anatomy).subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy

Clivus (anatomy).fact: In 2023, variant tubercles and eminences have been found on the basilar surface of the clivus in around 10% of the general population.

Clivus (anatomy).subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Clivus (anatomy).question: When viewed on a lateral C-spine radiograph, the clivus forms a line which, if extended, is known as _____'s clivus line
Clivus (anatomy).fact: When viewed on a lateral C-spine radiograph, the clivus forms a line which, if extended, is called Wackenheim's clivus line. Wackenheim's clivus line should pass through the dens of the axis or be tangential to it.

Clivus (anatomy).subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Clivus (anatomy).question: To disambiguate, the clivus is sometimes referred to as the _____ clivus
Clivus (anatomy).fact: To disambiguate, the clivus is sometimes called the Blumenbach clivus. This is named after Johann Friedrich Blumenbach.

Acidophil cell.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Acidophil cell.question: The _____ was Cell type found in the pituitary gland.
Acidophil cell.fact: In the anterior pituitary, the term "acidophil" is used to describe two different types of cells which stain well with acidic dyes. Somatotrophs, which secrete growth hormone (a peptide hormone) Lactotrophs, which secrete prolactin (a peptide hormone) When using standard staining techniques, they cannot be distinguished from each other (though they can be distinguished from basophils and chromophobes), and are therefore identified simply as "acidophils".

Adrenal medulla.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Adrenal medulla.question: The _____ was Central part of the adrenal gland.
Adrenal medulla.fact: The adrenal medulla (Latin: medulla glandulae suprarenalis) is the inner part of the adrenal gland.

Adrenal medulla.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Adrenal medulla.question: Adrenaline composes about _____ of the released catecholamines, and noradrenaline the other 15%
Adrenal medulla.fact: Adrenaline composes about 85% of the released catecholamines, and noradrenaline the other 15%.

Alpha cell.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Alpha cell.question: The _____ was Glucagon secreting cell.
Alpha cell.fact: Alpha cells (α-cells) are endocrine cells that are found in the Islets of Langerhans in the pancreas. Alpha cells secrete the peptide hormone glucagon in order to increase glucose levels in the blood stream.

Alpha cell.question: Laguesse discovered that the cells within the Islets of _____ contained granules that distinguished them from acini cells
Alpha cell.fact: This same year, Édouard Laguesse named them after Langerhans. Laguesse discovered that the cells within the Islets of Langerhans contained granules that distinguished them from acini cells.

Alpha cell.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Alpha cell.question: As the intracellular concentration of cAMP rises, protein kinase A (PKA) is activated and phosphorylates the transcription factor cAMP _____ (CREB) protein
Alpha cell.fact: As the intracellular concentration of cAMP rises, protein kinase A (PKA) is activated and phosphorylates the transcription factor cAMP Response Element Binding (CREB) protein.

Alpha cell.fact: CREB then induces transcription of glucose-6-phosphatase and phosphoenolpyruvate carboxylase (PEPCK).

Alpha cell.fact: PKA also phosphorylates phospho-fructokinase 2 (PFK2)/fructose 2,6-biphsophatase (FBPase2), inhibiting PFK2 and activating FBPase2.

Alpha cell.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Alpha cell.question: Parasympathetic control of the pancreas appears to originate from the _____ nerve
Alpha cell.fact: Parasympathetic control of the pancreas appears to originate from the Vagus nerve. Electrical and pharmacological stimulation of the Vagus nerve increases secretion of glucagon and insulin in most mammalian species, including humans.

Alpha cell.fact: Parasympathetic control of the pancreas appears to originate from the Vagus nerve. Electrical and pharmacological stimulation of the Vagus nerve increases secretion of glucagon and insulin in most mammalian species, including humans.

Alpha cell.fact: It is not entirely clear why glucagon levels are so high in patients with Type II diabetes.

Alpha cell.fact: In 1921, Banting and Best were testing pancreatic extracts in dogs that had had their pancreas removed. They discovered that "insulin-induced hypoglycemia was preceded by a transient, rather mild hyperglycemia..." Murlin is credited with the discovery of glucagon because in 1923 they suggested that the early hyperglycemic effect observed by Banting and Best was due to "a contaminant with glucogenic properties that they also proposed to call 'glucagon,' or the mobilizer of glucose".

Basophil cell.question: (It is usually not possible to distinguish between these cell types using standard staining techniques.) *_____ only in pregnancy by the developing embryo
Basophil cell.fact: (It is usually not possible to distinguish between these cell types using standard staining techniques.) *Produced only in pregnancy by the developing embryo.

Beta cell.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Beta cell.question: The _____ was Type of cell found in pancreatic islets.
Beta cell.fact: Beta cells (β-cells) are specialized endocrine cells located within the pancreatic islets of Langerhans responsible for the production and release of insulin and amylin. Constituting ~50–70% of cells in human islets, beta cells play a vital role in maintaining blood glucose levels.

Beta cell.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Beta cell.question: Subsequent to protein folding, proinsulin is transported to the _____ apparatus and enters immature insulin granules where proinsulin is cleaved to form insulin and C-peptide
Beta cell.fact: Subsequent to protein folding, proinsulin is transported to the Golgi apparatus and enters immature insulin granules where proinsulin is cleaved to form insulin and C-peptide.

Beta cell.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Beta cell.question: This system of release is commonly referred to as glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (_____)
Beta cell.fact: This system of release is commonly called glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS). There are four key events to the triggering pathway of GSIS: GLUT dependent glucose uptake, glucose metabolism, KATP channel closure, and the opening of voltage gated calcium channels causing insulin granule fusion and exocytosis.

Beta cell.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Beta cell.question: Under non-glucose stimulated conditions, the _____ channels are open and the voltage gated calcium channels are closed
Beta cell.fact: There are four key events to the triggering pathway of GSIS: GLUT dependent glucose uptake, glucose metabolism, KATP channel closure, and the opening of voltage gated calcium channels causing insulin granule fusion and exocytosis. Voltage-gated calcium channels and ATP-sensitive potassium ion channels (KATP channels) are embedded in the plasma membrane of beta cells.

Beta cell.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Beta cell.question: When the glucose concentration outside the cell is high, glucose molecules move into the cell by facilitated diffusion, down its concentration gradient through glucose transporters (_____)
Beta cell.fact: When the glucose concentration outside the cell is high, glucose molecules move into the cell by facilitated diffusion, down its concentration gradient through glucose transporters (GLUT). Rodent beta cells primarily express the GLUT2 isoform, whereas human beta cells, although also expressing GLUT2, mainly make use of GLUT1 and GLUT3 isoforms.

Beta cell.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Beta cell.question: The _____ channels close when the ATP to ADP ratio rises
Beta cell.fact: The KATP channels close when the ATP to ADP ratio rises. The closure of the KATP channels causes the outward potassium ion current to diminish, leading to inward currents of potassium ions dominating.

Beta cell.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Beta cell.question: The closure of the _____ channels causes the outward potassium ion current to diminish, leading to inward currents of potassium ions dominating
Beta cell.fact: The KATP channels close when the ATP to ADP ratio rises. The closure of the KATP channels causes the outward potassium ion current to diminish, leading to inward currents of potassium ions dominating.

Beta cell.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Beta cell.question: Amylin, also known as islet amyloid polypeptide (_____)

Beta cell.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Beta cell.question: Constituting ~50–_____ of cells in human islets, beta cells play a vital role in maintaining blood glucose levels
Beta cell.fact: Constituting ~50–70% of cells in human islets, beta cells play a vital role in maintaining blood glucose levels.

Beta cell.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Beta cell.question: The body destroys 70–_____ of beta cells, leaving only 20–30% of functioning cells
Beta cell.fact: The body destroys 70–80% of beta cells, leaving only 20–30% of functioning cells.

Beta cell.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Beta cell.question: However, the beta cells can become overworked and exhausted from being overstimulated, leading to a _____ reduction in function along with a 40% decrease in beta-cell volume
Beta cell.fact: However, the beta cells can become overworked and exhausted from being overstimulated, leading to a 50% reduction in function along with a 40% decrease in beta-cell volume.

Buster Gonad.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy

Buster Gonad.fact: Buster also featured in the 1991 Viz computer game. During the Gulf War of 1991, a SEPECAT Jaguar GR1A (number XZ118 Y) bomber of the Royal Air Force featured Buster Gonad nose art.

Chromaffin cell.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Chromaffin cell.question: The _____ was Neuroendocrine cells found in adrenal medulla in mammals.
Chromaffin cell.fact: Chromaffin cells, also called pheochromocytes (or phaeochromocytes), are neuroendocrine cells found mostly in the medulla of the adrenal glands in mammals. In order to activate chromaffin cells, the splanchnic nerve of the sympathetic nervous system releases acetylcholine, which then binds to nicotinic acetylcholine receptors on the adrenal medulla.

Chromophobe cell.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Chromophobe cell.question: The _____ was Cell type.
Chromophobe cell.fact: A chromophobe cell is a cell that does not stain readily, and thus appears relatively pale under the microscope. Chromophobe cells are one of three cell stain types present in the anterior and intermediate lobes of the pituitary gland, the others being basophilic and acidophilic.

Basilar skull fracture.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Basilar skull fracture.question: The _____ was Bone breakage in the base of the skull.
Basilar skull fracture.fact: A basilar skull fracture is a break of a bone in the base of the skull.

Battle's sign.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Battle's sign.question: The _____ was Bruises behind the ears, indicating skull fracture.
Battle's sign.fact: Battle's sign, also called mastoid ecchymosis or Postauricular ecchymosis, is a late indication of fracture of middle cranial fossa of the skull, appearing as bruising over one or both of the mastoid processes at least one day after the injury. Battle's sign is considered a late sign, as it takes at least one day to appear after the initial traumatic basilar skull fracture, similar to raccoon eyes.

Battle's sign.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Battle's sign.question: The sign is named after _____
Battle's sign.fact: The sign is named after William Henry Battle.
